o1.biggest_strength: It turns the strongest data signal into the main save by bringing back the 1-month pause, and it gives product-ready copy for each reason path.
o1.biggest_mistake: It keeps an unproven 50% discount for people switching apps and counts that as upside, when the brief points away from discount-led saving.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove or test-gate the switching-app discount, tighten the revenue assumptions around discounted users, and make the pause the clear first build priority.

o2.biggest_strength: It clearly acts on the main signals: restore the pause, stop wasting discounts on trip completers, move price-sensitive monthly users to annual, and treat lack of progress as a reminder problem.
o2.biggest_mistake: It overstates the billing issue by saying the new billing system cannot do pause yet, and it lacks full confirmation copy for people who accept save offers.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add exact done-state copy for pause, annual switch and reminder acceptance, and soften the billing claim to match the data given.

reason: Output 2 is the one I would hand to the team first because it is more disciplined about removing discounts and puts the pause rebuild first. Output 1 is very usable, but the extra 50% offer for switchers feels like old-flow thinking creeping back in.
